daemon_restart_lesson.title: Daemon-restart-from-inside-orchestrator-cgroup is the single most disruptive recurring trap
daemon_restart_lesson.what_happened_in_cycle_2: Dev subagent restarted happy-daemon-dev.service as part of its BA-mandated cycle-2 workflow (after yarn build of new codexAppServerClient.ts + sessionProtocolMapper.ts). The restart disrupted the orchestrator's session because the orchestrator was running inside the daemon-managed cgroup. The user explicitly flagged this as disruptive and instructed: NO further daemon restarts in cycle 2. QA proceeded WITHOUT a second restart, verifying daemon health via curl /health + daemon.state.json read instead.
daemon_restart_lesson.root_cause: CLAUDE.md Critical Operational Rule 5: 'NEVER restart daemon from within a daemon-managed Claude session (cgroup kill).' The dev daemon's cgroup contains the orchestrator's Claude process; `systemctl restart happy-daemon-dev.service` SIGTERMs the entire cgroup, including the orchestrator. The architect cycle-2 report (arch-5) elevated this to a tier-1 issue and the BA spec correctly documented two cgroup-safe patterns (Pattern A: systemd-run --scope; Pattern B: nohup-detach), but in practice the restart still disrupted the session — apparently the cgroup-safe pattern was either not used or not sufficient on the first restart.
lesson_for_next_session: Pattern A (systemd-run --scope --collect from a separate shell) is the documented safe path. Verify it actually works on this server before relying on it again.
Pattern B (nohup bash -c 'sleep 2 && systemctl restart happy-daemon-dev.service' < /dev/null > /dev/null 2>&1 &) is the documented fallback. Same caveat — verify behavior empirically.

Alternative approach: SCHEDULE the daemon restart for AFTER the orchestrator session ends. The cycle's Dev work proceeds through yarn build → bundle deploy; QA accepts source+bundle+typecheck without requiring a live restart in-cycle. The user (or a manual operator) restarts post-session.
Alternative approach: orchestrator detects when its own session is in the dev cgroup and refuses to delegate any task that requires daemon restart, instead emitting an escalation to the user.

If a daemon restart MUST happen in-cycle, the orchestrator should checkpoint state before delegating to Dev, and have a recovery-friendly resume plan that re-reads daemon state on resume (e.g. read /root/.happy-dev/daemon.state.json to recover pid + httpPort + version).
daemon_restart_lesson.policy_for_future_cycles: Prefer non-disrupting restart pattern (cgroup-safe systemd-run --scope from a separate shell) OR accept the disruption with a recovery-friendly orchestration plan that re-reads daemon state on resume. Document the chosen pattern in the BA spec as an explicit step with the EXACT command, and require Dev to log the command used as evidence. QA must verify the command matches the cgroup-safe pattern.
daemon_restart_lesson.verification_for_next_session: When picking up §5.10 transport-layer (which also requires daemon rebuild + restart), the next session should test a single cgroup-safe restart command from a separate shell BEFORE writing the BA spec. If the command does not work cleanly, fall back to user-initiated restart post-session. Do NOT delegate restart to Dev without this verification.
